about.title: About IRA Calculator - Individual Retirement Account Planning Tool
about.description: The IRA Calculator is a comprehensive retirement planning tool designed to help you calculate the growth potential of your Individual Retirement Account investments. Whether you're planning for Traditional IRA or Roth IRA contributions, this calculator provides accurate projections of your retirement savings growth over time. Understanding IRA calculations is essential for maximizing your retirement savings and making informed decisions about contribution limits, tax benefits, and withdrawal strategies.

faq.q: What's the difference between Traditional and Roth IRA?
faq.a: Traditional IRA contributions may be tax-deductible now, but withdrawals in retirement are taxed as income. Roth IRA contributions are made with after-tax dollars, but qualified withdrawals in retirement are tax-free.

faq.q: What are the 2024 IRA contribution limits?
faq.a: For 2024, you can contribute up to $7,000 to an IRA ($8,000 if you're 50 or older). These limits apply to the total of all your IRA contributions, whether Traditional or Roth.

faq.q: When can I withdraw from my IRA without penalties?
faq.a: You can withdraw IRA funds penalty-free starting at age 59½. Early withdrawals before this age typically incur a 10% penalty, though some exceptions exist for first-time home purchases, education expenses, and medical costs.

faq.q: Do I have to take required minimum distributions from my IRA?
faq.a: Traditional IRAs require minimum distributions starting at age 73. Roth IRAs have no required distributions during the owner's lifetime, making them excellent for estate planning.
